description.Tyrannosaurus rex: Giant theropod with tiny arms and a bite stronger than that of any other land animal.
description.Triceratops horridus: Herbivore with three facial horns and a large bony frill, the tyrannosaur's natural rival.
description.Velociraptor mongoliensis: Small feathered hunter with a retractable sickle-shaped claw on each foot.
description.Stegosaurus stenops: Herbivore with bony plates along its back and defensive spikes on its tail.
description.Brachiosaurus altithorax: Extremely long-necked sauropod whose front legs were longer than its hind legs.
description.Diplodocus carnegii: Sauropod with an extremely long neck and tail and a slender body.
description.Spinosaurus aegyptiacus: Theropod with a large dorsal sail and a long, crocodile-like snout.
description.Ankylosaurus magniventris: Armored herbivore with a bony club on its tail.
description.Parasaurolophus walkeri: Hadrosaur with a hollow tubular head crest it used to communicate.
description.Allosaurus fragilis: Jurassic theropod with bony crests above its eyes and three-fingered claws.
description.Iguanodon bernissartensis: Herbivore with a spike-shaped thumb and a horny beak.
description.Argentinosaurus huinculensis: One of the largest land animals in history, a South American sauropod.
description.Giganotosaurus carolinii: South American theropod larger than the tyrannosaur, with shark-like teeth.
description.Compsognathus longipes: One of the smallest non-avian dinosaurs, about the size of a chicken.
description.Archaeopteryx lithographica: Considered the oldest known bird, with feathers and teeth.
description.Therizinosaurus cheloniformis: Theropod with giant claws nearly a meter long on its hands.
description.Protoceratops andrewsi: Small ceratopsian without large horns and with a modest bony frill.
description.Pachycephalosaurus wyomingensis: Biped with a domed skull of solid bone, probably used for head-butting.
description.Dilophosaurus wetherilli: Theropod with two semicircular crests on its head.
description.Carnotaurus sastrei: Theropod with two small horns and ridiculously short arms.
description.Apatosaurus ajax: Robust Jurassic sauropod with a whip-like tail.
description.Plateosaurus engelhardti: Early Triassic prosauropod, one of the first large herbivores.
description.Coelophysis bauri: Slender, lightweight Triassic theropod, an agile hunter that lived in groups.
description.Utahraptor ostrommaysi: The largest known dromaeosaurid, with sickle-shaped claws.
description.Styracosaurus albertensis: Ceratopsian with a long nasal horn and several horns on its frill.
description.Corythosaurus casuarius: Hadrosaur with a crest shaped like a Corinthian helmet.
description.Edmontosaurus annectens: Duck-billed hadrosaur, one of the last non-avian dinosaurs.
description.Deinonychus antirrhopus: Dromaeosaurid that inspired the velociraptor in Jurassic Park.
description.Maiasaura peeblesorum: Hadrosaur famous for caring for its young in nests.
description.Oviraptor philoceratops: Theropod with a toothless beak and a crest; its name means 'egg thief'.
description.Baryonyx walkeri: European spinosaurid with a large curved claw on its thumb.
description.Gallimimus bullatus: Fast-running theropod with long legs and an ostrich-like appearance.
description.Kentrosaurus aethiopicus: African stegosaurid with spikes instead of plates on its hips and tail.
description.Ceratosaurus nasicornis: Theropod with a horn on its nose and crests above its eyes.
description.Massospondylus carinatus: Early sauropod with large thumbs, one of the first dinosaurs ever described.
description.Suchomimus tenerensis: African spinosaurid with a long, crocodile-like snout.
description.Camarasaurus lentus: Robust sauropod with a short skull and spoon-shaped teeth.
description.Herrerasaurus ischigualastensis: One of the oldest carnivorous dinosaurs, from the South American Triassic.
description.Scelidosaurus harrisonii: Early thyreophoran with armor of bony scutes, an ancestor of the ankylosaurs.
description.Microraptor gui: Tiny dromaeosaurid with four feathered wings.
description.Carcharodontosaurus saharicus: African theropod with sharp, shark-like teeth.
description.Patagotitan mayorum: One of the largest animals that ever lived, an Argentine sauropod.
description.Mamenchisaurus constructus: Asian sauropod with the longest neck relative to its body.
description.Amargasaurus cazaui: Sauropod with two rows of tall spines along its neck.
description.Nigersaurus taqueti: Sauropod with more than 500 teeth and a skull adapted for grazing at ground level.
description.Euoplocephalus tutus: Ankylosaurid with a tail club and armored eyelids.
description.Tuojiangosaurus multispinus: Asian stegosaurid with triangular plates and spikes.
description.Lambeosaurus lambei: Hadrosaur with a bony, hatchet-shaped crest on its head.
description.Shantungosaurus giganteus: The largest known hadrosaur, as big as a tyrannosaur.
description.Deinocheirus mirificus: Humpbacked omnivorous theropod with enormous arms and claws.
description.Ouranosaurus nigeriensis: African ornithopod with a dorsal sail similar to the spinosaur's.
description.Torosaurus latus: Ceratopsian with one of the largest skulls of any land animal.
description.Pentaceratops sternbergii: Ceratopsian with five horns (two true horns and three on the frill).
description.Centrosaurus apertus: Ceratopsian with a single large nasal horn and a short frill.
description.Pachyrhinosaurus canadensis: Ceratopsian with a large bony boss instead of a nasal horn.
description.Dromaeosaurus albertensis: Small North American dromaeosaurid, the one that gave the group its name.
description.Abelisaurus comahuensis: South American theropod with a short skull and a blunt snout.
description.Majungasaurus crenatissimus: Malagasy theropod with a rounded horn on its forehead and cannibalistic habits.
description.Sinosauropteryx prima: Small Chinese theropod, the first to show clear evidence of feathers.
description.Stygimoloch spinifer: Pachycephalosaur with spikes on the back of its skull.
description.Cryolophosaurus ellioti: Predator from the frozen continent with a sideways crest on its head that looks like a quiff.
description.Australovenator wintonensis: Agile, lightly built hunter from Queensland with long claws on its hands.
description.Mapusaurus roseae: Patagonian giant found in a bonebed with several individuals together, hinting at group hunting.
description.Tarbosaurus bataar: Asian cousin of the tyrant king, apex predator of the Gobi with even smaller arms.
description.Yutyrannus huali: Large Chinese tyrannosauroid covered in long feather-like filaments.
description.Concavenator corcovatus: Carnivore from Cuenca, Spain, with a strange pointed hump above its hips.
description.Irritator challengeri: Brazilian spinosaurid whose skull was doctored with plaster by fossil dealers, to scientists' annoyance.
description.Sinraptor dongi: Large Jurassic predator from China whose skull bears bite marks from its own kind.
description.Guanlong wucaii: Early relative of the tyrannosaurs with a showy hollow crest along its snout.
description.Neovenator salerii: Large carnivore from the Isle of Wight with a highly sensitive, nerve-rich snout.
description.Monolophosaurus jiangi: Theropod from the Junggar Basin with a single bony crest running along its skull.
description.Megalosaurus bucklandii: The first non-avian dinosaur ever given a scientific name, described in England.
description.Torvosaurus tanneri: One of the largest carnivores of the Jurassic, with short, powerful arms.
description.Eustreptospondylus oxoniensis: English predator with well-curved vertebrae that may have lived on islands.
description.Rugops primus: Saharan abelisaurid with a wrinkled face, probably a scavenger.
description.Austroraptor cabazai: Large Patagonian raptor with a long snout and conical teeth, perhaps a fish-eater.
description.Buitreraptor gonzalezorum: Small Argentine dromaeosaurid with a very slender snout, found at a site called La Buitrera.
description.Halszkaraptor escuilliei: Mongolian raptor with a swan-like neck and flipper-like arms that may have swum like a duck.
description.Mononykus olecranus: Small Mongolian runner with stubby arms ending in a single stout claw, ideal for termite mounds.
description.Gigantoraptor erlianensis: Colossal toothless-beaked oviraptorosaur, as large as a mid-sized tyrannosaur.
description.Citipati osmolskae: Famous for fossils found brooding their eggs with arms spread over the nest.
description.Caudipteryx zoui: Turkey-sized feathered dinosaur with a fan of feathers on its tail.
description.Struthiomimus altus: Fast runner shaped like an ostrich, with a toothless beak and long legs.
description.Ornithomimus velox: North American runner whose name means "bird mimic", with feathered wings in adults.
description.Saurornitholestes langstoni: Coyote-sized Canadian dromaeosaurid, sometimes mistaken for its Mongolian cousin.
description.Bambiraptor feinbergi: Small Montana raptor found by a 14-year-old boy and named after a cartoon fawn.
description.Nothronychus mckinleyi: Pot-bellied plant-eating theropod from New Mexico with huge claws and a sloth-like look.
description.Falcarius utahensis: Link between meat-eating theropods and plant-eating therizinosaurs, known from thousands of bones in Utah.
description.Albertosaurus sarcophagus: Canadian tyrannosaurid found in a bonebed holding more than twenty individuals.
description.Gorgosaurus libratus: Slender tyrannosaurid from Alberta, the most common of its family in the fossil record.
description.Daspletosaurus torosus: Robust tyrannosaurid whose name means "frightful lizard".
description.Lythronax argestes: Short-snouted tyrannosaurid from Utah, the "gore king", older than its famous relative.
description.Qianzhousaurus sinensis: Chinese tyrannosaurid with a long narrow snout, nicknamed after a famous wooden puppet.
description.Aucasaurus garridoi: Patagonian abelisaurid known from a nearly complete skeleton, with tiny arms.
description.Elaphrosaurus bambergi: Slender, lightweight, long-legged theropod from Tanzania.
description.Limusaurus inextricabilis: Small Chinese theropod that lost its teeth as it grew, ending up with a beak.
description.Masiakasaurus knopfleri: Small Malagasy predator with forward-jutting front teeth, named after a rock guitarist.
description.Staurikosaurus pricei: One of the oldest dinosaurs, a small hunter from Brazil.
description.Acrocanthosaurus atokensis: Large carnivore from Oklahoma with a tall ridge of spines along its back.
description.Ornitholestes hermanni: Small Jurassic hunter from Wyoming whose name means "bird robber".
description.Eoraptor lunensis: Tiny early dinosaur from the Valley of the Moon in Argentina.
description.Mussaurus patagonicus: First known from hatchlings so small it was named the "mouse lizard".
description.Lufengosaurus huenei: Early sauropodomorph from Yunnan, the first dinosaur skeleton mounted in China.
description.Shunosaurus lii: Moderately long-necked sauropod with a small bony club at the end of its tail.
description.Saltasaurus loricatus: Relatively small titanosaur with its back covered in bony armour plates.
description.Dreadnoughtus schrani: Gigantic Patagonian titanosaur with a very complete skeleton that "fears nothing".
description.Supersaurus vivianae: Diplodocid from Colorado, one of the longest dinosaurs known.
description.Giraffatitan brancai: Tanzanian sauropod with a very upright neck, the huge mounted skeleton in Berlin.
description.Europasaurus holgeri: Dwarf sauropod from an island in what is now Germany, the size of a large horse.
description.Magyarosaurus dacus: Dwarf titanosaur from Hațeg Island in what is now Romania, only a few metres long.
description.Ampelosaurus atacis: Armoured titanosaur from southern France, found among vineyards.
description.Barosaurus lentus: Very long-necked diplodocid, mounted rearing on its hind legs in New York.
description.Sauroposeidon proteles: Oklahoma sauropod with neck vertebrae so big they were first mistaken for fossil tree trunks.
description.Alamosaurus sanjuanensis: Last giant sauropod of North America, a contemporary of the tyrant king.
description.Cetiosaurus oxoniensis: English sauropod described in 1841 as a marine "whale lizard".
description.Turiasaurus riodevensis: Giant sauropod from Teruel, Spain, one of the largest dinosaurs of Europe.
description.Riojasaurus incertus: Heavy, four-legged Triassic sauropodomorph from La Rioja, Argentina.
description.Sauropelta edwardsorum: Montana nodosaur with large spikes along the sides of its neck.
description.Polacanthus foxii: English ankylosaur with a solid bony shield over its hips and spikes along its sides.
description.Zuul crurivastator: Montana ankylosaurid named after a movie monster, with a "shin-destroyer" tail club.
description.Borealopelta markmitchelli: Canadian nodosaur preserved like a statue, with skin and pigments intact.
description.Edmontonia longiceps: Armoured nodosaur with large shoulder spikes and no tail club.
description.Diamantinasaurus matildae: Sturdy titanosaur from Queensland, found together with a predator nicknamed "Banjo".
description.Pinacosaurus grangeri: Gobi ankylosaurid found in groups of juveniles buried together by sandstorms.
description.Saichania chulsanensis: Mongolian ankylosaurid with a heavily armoured skull whose name means "beautiful".
description.Dacentrurus armatus: Large European stegosaur with spikes instead of plates along much of its back.
description.Hesperosaurus mjosi: Stegosaur from Wyoming and Montana with lower, longer back plates than its famous relative.
description.Huayangosaurus taibaii: Small, early Chinese stegosaur with spikes on its shoulders.
description.Scutellosaurus lawleri: Small two-legged armoured dinosaur from Arizona with hundreds of bony scutes in its skin.
description.Psittacosaurus mongoliensis: Two-legged ceratopsian with a parrot beak and tail bristles, one of the dinosaurs with the most fossils.
description.Leptoceratops gracilis: Small hornless ceratopsian that lived alongside its gigantic relatives.
description.Chasmosaurus belli: Ceratopsian from Alberta with a huge frill pierced by large openings.
description.Einiosaurus procurvicornis: Montana centrosaur with a nose horn curved downward like a bottle opener.
description.Kosmoceratops richardsoni: Utah ceratopsian with fifteen horns, the most ornate skull of any dinosaur.
description.Nasutoceratops titusi: Big-nosed ceratopsian with long horns curved like those of a bull.
description.Regaliceratops peterhewsi: Canadian ceratopsian with a crown-shaped frill, nicknamed after a comic-book hero.
description.Sinoceratops zhuchengensis: The first large ceratopsid found in China, with curved hooks on its frill.
description.Yinlong downsi: One of the oldest ceratopsians, small and two-legged, found while a film was being shot nearby.
description.Stegoceras validum: Small pachycephalosaur with a smooth, thick domed skull.
description.Prenocephale prenes: Mongolian pachycephalosaur with a rounded dome ringed by small knobs.
description.Hypsilophodon foxii: Small, fast plant-eater from the Isle of Wight, once wrongly imagined climbing trees.
description.Tenontosaurus tilletti: Very long-tailed ornithopod, a frequent prey of a famous pack-hunting raptor.
description.Dryosaurus altus: Agile Jurassic ornithopod with long legs and a horny beak, the "oak lizard".
description.Camptosaurus dispar: Sturdy Jurassic ornithopod that could walk on two or four legs.
description.Lesothosaurus diagnosticus: Small, early running ornithischian from southern Africa.
description.Heterodontosaurus tucki: Small South African ornithischian with three kinds of teeth, including tusks.
description.Muttaburrasaurus langdoni: Australian ornithopod with a hollow bony bump on its snout.
description.Leaellynasaura amicagraphica: Small plant-eater of Australia's polar forests, with big eyes and a very long tail.
description.Hypacrosaurus altispinus: Hollow-crested hadrosaur with tall back spines, known from nests and embryos.
description.Saurolophus osborni: Hadrosaur with a solid spike-like crest pointing backwards.
description.Olorotitan arharensis: Long-necked Russian hadrosaur with a hatchet-shaped crest, the "swan titan".
description.Tsintaosaurus spinorhinus: Chinese hadrosaur nicknamed the "unicorn" for the crest jutting from its head.
description.Gryposaurus notabilis: Hook-nosed hadrosaur with a big nasal arch, the "griffin-nosed lizard".
description.Brachylophosaurus canadensis: Short, flat-crested hadrosaur, famous for a mummy nicknamed "Leonardo".
description.Thescelosaurus neglectus: Sturdy ornithopod from the very end of the Cretaceous, whose "fossil heart" made headlines.
